page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-60 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 9B14 processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine provides 60 dedicated vCPUs spanning 30 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem is configured with 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with support for vector extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Memory capacity is provisioned at 118 GB, yielding approximately 1.97 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, requiring network-attached persistent storage for filesystem needs, and no discrete GPUs are included.

Benchmark results highlight strong multithreaded compute throughput. The instance achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,625 and a PassMark CPU score of 68,289.24, ranking in the top tier for multi-core processing. Performance is particularly high in parallel tasks, demonstrated by strong Geekbench scores in software compilation via Clang (50,490) and ray tracing (70,724). Vector-accelerated instruction tests in PassMark reached 75,379.8, benefiting from modern AVX instruction sets. Memory performance is solid in cached scenarios with 4,252.27 GB/sec small-block read bandwidth, while uncached large-block throughput settles into typical mid-tier ranges at 146.01 GB/sec read and 53.0 GB/sec write.

With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance optimizes cost efficiency for compute-bound operations rather than data footprints requiring large in-memory caches. Workload suitability centers on parallel batch compute, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, static or web microservices, and CPU-based machine learning inference, where small and medium parameter models exhibit strong token generation throughput.

It provides 60 dedicated vCPUs across 30 physical cores with multithreading, alongside 118 GB of system memory, averaging 1.97 GB per vCPU. The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. No local disk storage or discrete GPUs are bundled with the hardware configuration. Uncached memory throughput and single-threaded operations perform in the median range. This compute-to-memory density makes the instance effective for compute-heavy parallel workloads, automated build pipelines, CPU-driven inference tasks, and distributed batch processing.
